# Quaestor

> An AI orchestration platform: governed delegation of work to Execution Agents, with
> independent evidence instead of self-reported success.

Quaestor has two orchestration modes. They are not layered: Relay Mode does not run through
Program Mode. They share one substrate -- authority, evidence, repository observation and
classification.

**Relay Mode** keeps a selected Orchestrator and a selected Execution Agent in one continuous
governed conversation with no copy/paste (`quaestor relay start`; also `resume`, `status`,
`doctor`, `stop`). Quaestor carries every turn, reads the repository itself rather than
believing the agent's account of its own work, and gates effects: a directive reaching for an
effect the operator has not granted stops the relay and interrupts a human. Relay traffic is
natural prose, not a JSON schema.

**Program Mode** runs a loop: an operator creates a **program** with an objective and acceptance
criteria; a planner attaches **lanes** (steps); `tick` admits at-most-one execution per dispatch
identity, hands the executor an authority envelope plus a task, and reads back a single JSON
**handoff** whose claims are reconciled against independently measured evidence; messages pause
and resume lanes; nothing advances on chat alone.

In both modes, authority is granted by humans through a governed vocabulary and is enforced
outside the executor's reach.

## Agent entry points

- [docs/PRD.md](docs/PRD.md) -- the canonical product contract. Where this repository and the
  PRD disagree about what the product IS, the PRD governs.
- [.well-known/quaestor-agent.json](.well-known/quaestor-agent.json) -- machine-readable contract:
  protocol version, surfaces, adapter modes (available vs planned), completion contract,
  authority rules.
- [skills/quaestor/SKILL.md](skills/quaestor/SKILL.md) -- instructions for an agent connecting
  itself: discover state read-only, receive a task, satisfy the completion contract, escalate
  correctly, and what changes when you are inside a relay instead.
- [docs/RELAY-MODE.md](docs/RELAY-MODE.md) -- Relay Mode: the topology, the kernel's guarantees,
  the endpoints that are qualified today, and how effects are governed.
- [docs/OPERATIONS.md](docs/OPERATIONS.md) -- installation, deployment home, execution modes,
  owner channel: every command grounded in the real CLI.

Status is stated honestly throughout: anything not built yet is labelled **planned**, not implied.
Capability is reported on a maturity ladder -- IMPLEMENTED, TEST_QUALIFIED,
LIVE_PROVIDER_QUALIFIED, LIVE_END_TO_END_QUALIFIED, PRODUCT_SUPPORTED -- so "it works" and "you
can rely on it" stay separate claims.

## Quaestor Core

`quaestor serve` runs Quaestor Core: an authenticated loopback service boundary that future
clients (a browser extension, a web UI, a tray) reach INSTEAD of reaching the machine. It is not
a new execution path -- it reads the same durable stores the CLI writes.

The API is five named operations (`core.status`, `core.identity`, `projects.list`, `relay.list`,
`relay.status`) plus an unauthenticated `GET /health`. There is deliberately no execute, no file
read or write, and no path parameter: a project is named by its id, and a client token is scoped
to named projects. See docs/OPERATIONS.md section 12.
